summary: Los Padres NF lookout begun 1935; original cab burned in 1948, a relocated replacement burned in the 1970s; only the steel frame stands (2012 and 2017 accounts).

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-302 cab on a 10-foot enclosed timber tower (structure lost in 1948, per registry)
facts.status_note: Only the steel frame remains; the cab was lost in the 1970s. Carey (2012) and a 2017 trail write-up both describe the frame.

access.note: On foot only. Carey describes a seven-mile approach via the Gridley Trail; the 2017 write-up describes about 12 miles round trip from Ojai via Pratt Trail.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Los Padres National Forest

visit.trail_note: Approach is on foot: seven miles via the Gridley Trail (Carey, 2012), or about 12 miles round trip from Ojai via Pratt Trail (2017 write-up).

events.note: Forest Service started work on a lookout station (newspaper, June 20, 1935). Completion date not found in the sources read.
Observer John V. Tracy on duty at Nordhoff Lookout; reported a smoke later found to be a house fire in North Hollywood (newspaper, Sept 1938)
Wheeler Springs Fire (Carey) destroyed the original wooden cab; newspaper of Sept 17, 1948 says a fire burned the lookout tower and does not name it
An existing tower and cabin were relocated by helicopter from Rincon Mountain, circa 1950
Forest Service operated a Ground Observer Corps post out of the lookout (newspaper, Nov 14, 1956)
Registered December 19, 2019; nominated by Brad Eells

corrections.why: The only height in the sources is a 10-foot enclosed timber tower for the structure lost in 1948. No source we read gives a height for the current steel frame, so 152.4 m is unsupported.

corrections.proposed: 1935 built (work started); c.1950 relocated tower and cabin
corrections.why: A June 1935 newspaper report shows work on a lookout began in 1935. The circa 1950 date is for the relocated replacement that followed the 1948 fire.
The brief lists only one loss. The original cab burned in 1948, and the replacement burned in the 1970s.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief's FFLA note says the tower stands with its cab gone; the registry says the site was not replaced; Carey (2012) and the 2017 write-up describe only the steel frame. Recorded as standing, steel frame only.
Carey names the 1948 fire the Wheeler Springs Fire; the 1948 newspaper quote does not name it. Linking the two is unconfirmed.

notes_for_editor: Current condition rests on a 2012 blog and a 2017 hiking write-up; no 2020s source was read. The Ojai Valley News article returned HTTP 429 twice and firelookouthost.org returned 404, so ffla_groups 'ruins' (brief) is unchecked. Height 152.4 m removed as unsupported. The replacement's loss is recorded only as 'the 1970s' in the sources, so no year event is listed for it. 1935 is the start of construction per a newspaper; completion year not found. Staffing after 1956 not found.
